narrative.overview:
Every number on screen has to be traceable to the transaction that produced it. The interface's job is not to summarise fuel consumption attractively — it is to show exactly how much of the total it can stand behind and to put the unaccounted remainder one click away. Where a conventional dashboard would round a gap away, this one names it: 28 codes · 47,624 L unassigned, linked straight to the registry that resolves them.

That purpose sets the density and the restraint. Surfaces are flat white cards on a cool slate canvas, separated by a single hairline rule, because anything more would be decoration competing with figures that end up in a council report. Exactly one saturated colour exists in the chrome — Action Blue — and it means "you can act here". The sidebar is ink in both light and dark, so the frame of the application never moves while the data inside it changes.

The two rejected worlds are on record. An earlier industrial black-and-yellow direction ("Hudson 8") was abandoned and must not be picked back up. The generic SaaS dashboard — gradient hero tiles, purple-blue accents, rounded-everything, emoji section markers — is the default this system exists in opposition to.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, hairline borders, no shadow anywhere
One saturated accent in the chrome; colour otherwise belongs to data
Figures in tabular numerals, grouped, with a non-breaking space before the unit
Uppercase micro-labels at 12px with wide tracking, never below that floor
Ink sidebar in both themes; the frame holds still
Exceptions are surfaced and linked, never smoothed

rules.name: The One Action Colour Rule
rules.body: Action Blue is the only saturated hue in the chrome. If a new element needs attention and is not actionable, it earns it through weight, size, or position — never by introducing a second accent.

rules.name: The Data-Chrome Separation Rule
rules.body: Series colours are for marks only. An interface element never borrows Petrol Blue or Diesel Orange, and a chart series never uses Action Blue. Cross the line and the reader stops being able to tell what is data and what is a control.

rules.name: The Measured Colour Rule
rules.body: Every series colour resolves from a CSS custom property through lib/chart-theme.ts. A hex literal in a chart component is a defect — it cannot follow the theme, and dark mode is where that shows.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text renders below 12px, anywhere, including SVG labels inside charts. Recharts tick and legend sizes are px on SVG and do not scale with the root, so they are set explicitly to 12 and checked separately.

rules.name: The Honest Root Rule
rules.body: The root font-size stays at the browser default. It was once pinned to 68% to buy density, which silently overrode every reader's own font-size preference and dropped body text to 10.88px. Density comes from spacing — padding, gaps, sidebar width — never from shrinking the root em.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Any digit that appears in a column gets tabular-nums. A number that shifts horizontally between rows cannot be scanned.

rules.name: The Container-Sized Figure Rule
rules.body: A headline figure is sized by the width of the card holding it, not by the viewport. Each KPI tile is a container query scope, stepping 18 → 20 → 24 → 30px as the card crosses 170/230/310px. A viewport breakpoint cannot distinguish a four-up row at 1280px from a three-up row at the same width.

rules.name: The No Side-Scroll Rule
rules.body: The page body never scrolls horizontally at any width down to 375px. Only tables, charts and code may exceed the column, each in its own overflow-x: auto container.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on any surface, in any state. If an element needs to separate from its neighbour, it gets a border or more space. A shadow added to signal interactivity is a sign the border and press states were not doing their job.

rules.name: The Press-Is-Feedback Rule
rules.body: Anything pressable compresses on :active. Buttons 0.97, large tiles 0.985, both over 160ms. On a surface where most actions wait on a database read, the press is the only immediate response the interface can give.

rules.name: The Repeated-Action Rule
rules.body: Controls used dozens of times an hour — filters, pagination, tab switches — get no entrance or exit animation. Motion on a repeated action reads as latency, not polish.

dos: Do route every displayed number through lib/format.ts, and every chart colour through lib/chart-theme.ts. One quantity reads identically on every screen and in every export, or the reader stops trusting all of it.
Do take the currency symbol from SystemSettings. A literal N$ goes stale the moment Settings changes while every figure around it updates.
Do state coverage as a measured share with a link to its exceptions.
Do keep issues (FIS) and receipts (FRE) visually distinct and never summed.
Do hold WCAG 2.1 AA: 4.5:1 on body text, 3:1 on large text and chart marks, keyboard reach for every drill-down, one visible h1 per route.
Do gate every hover style behind @media (hover: hover).
donts: Don't add a box-shadow to any surface, in any state.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent into the chrome, or use a series colour on an interface element.
Don't encode a categorical difference as two steps of one hue. Petrol and Diesel are different fuels, not more and less of one thing.
Don't colour a mark by its rank. A filter that changes the set must not repaint the survivors; sorted bars already encode rank by position.
Don't use transition-all, or any ease-in curve on an interface element.
Don't pin a font size in px where the rem scale would do, and never render text below 12px.
Don't put a coloured border wider than 1px on a card, list item or callout.
Don't drift toward the abandoned "Hudson 8" black-and-yellow industrial direction, or toward the generic SaaS dashboard look — gradient hero tiles, purple-blue accents, emoji section markers.
